snapshot.text: International Airlines Group, the owner of British Airways, Iberia, Aer Lingus and Vueling, ended FY2024 with revenue up {{revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{revenue@FY2024}} and both Moody's and S&P upgrading the group to investment grade during the year.

The EBITDA margin widened by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2024}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2024}} and net leverage fell by {{net_leverage.change@FY2024}} to {{net_leverage@FY2024}}, the lowest of the network peers.

The point to watch is customer prepayments: advance ticket cover fell by {{advance_ticket_cover.change@FY2024}} to {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2024}}, the weakest of the group, while undrawn committed facilities declined by {{undrawn_facilities.change@FY2024}} to {{undrawn_facilities@FY2024}}.

credit_metrics.text: EBITDA increased by {{ebitda.change@FY2024}} to {{ebitda@FY2024}}, and operating profit rose by {{operating_profit.change@FY2024}} to {{operating_profit@FY2024}} after depreciation.

Total debt rose by {{total_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{total_debt@FY2024}}, but net debt was reduced by {{net_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{net_debt@FY2024}} as cash built up, taking gross leverage down by {{gross_leverage.change@FY2024}} to {{gross_leverage@FY2024}}.
Interest coverage improved by {{interest_coverage.change@FY2024}} to {{interest_coverage@FY2024}}, well above the peer median of {{interest_coverage.peer_median@FY2024}}.

operating_performance.text: Capacity grew by {{ask.change@FY2024}} to {{ask@FY2024}} available seat kilometres, carrying {{passengers@FY2024}} passengers.

RASK rose by {{rask.change@FY2024}} to {{rask@FY2024}}, while CASK was broadly unchanged at {{cask@FY2024}} as the fuel share of costs fell by {{fuel_share_of_costs.change@FY2024}} to {{fuel_share_of_costs@FY2024}}.
CASK ex-fuel rose by {{cask_ex_fuel.change@FY2024}} to {{cask_ex_fuel@FY2024}}, so non-fuel unit costs absorbed part of the fuel benefit.

The fleet increased by {{fleet.change@FY2024}} to {{fleet@FY2024}} aircraft, with an average age of {{fleet_age@FY2024}}, as engine reliability issues and delivery delays continued to affect the group.

liquidity_funding.text: Liquidity rose by {{liquidity.change@FY2024}} to {{liquidity@FY2024}}, of which cash and cash-like investments of {{cash_like@FY2024}} were up {{cash_like.change@FY2024}}.
Cash liquidity to revenue rose by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}}, and liquidity to revenue reached {{liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}}.

Undrawn committed facilities fell by {{undrawn_facilities.change@FY2024}} to {{undrawn_facilities@FY2024}}, after the group replaced its previous secured facilities with a new sustainability-linked revolving credit facility that was undrawn at year end.

Contract liabilities rose by {{contract_liabilities.change@FY2024}} to {{contract_liabilities@FY2024}}, but advance ticket cover fell by {{advance_ticket_cover.change@FY2024}} to {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2024}}.

peer_positioning.text: IAG leads the network airlines on EBITDA margin ({{ebitda_margin.peer_rank@FY2024}}), net leverage ({{net_leverage.peer_rank@FY2024}}) and FFO to debt ({{ffo_to_debt.peer_rank@FY2024}}).

Advance ticket cover of {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2024}} is above the peer median of {{advance_ticket_cover.peer_median@FY2024}} yet ranks {{advance_ticket_cover.peer_rank@FY2024}}, the weakest of the group.
Capex intensity sits in the middle of the group, and FCF to debt of {{fcf_to_debt@FY2024}} is in line with the peer median of {{fcf_to_debt.peer_median@FY2024}}.

Undrawn facilities: committed lines fell by {{undrawn_facilities.change@FY2024}} to {{undrawn_facilities@FY2024}}, a weaker backstop than a year earlier.

Unit cost: CASK ex-fuel rose by {{cask_ex_fuel.change@FY2024}} to {{cask_ex_fuel@FY2024}}, so non-fuel costs are the pressure point even as the fuel share of costs fell to {{fuel_share_of_costs@FY2024}}.
Fleet: average age rose by {{fleet_age.change@FY2024}} to {{fleet_age@FY2024}} years, with engine reliability issues and delivery delays still affecting operations.
